actors.description: Male tennis player with dark hair, centre-frame on a dark blue court against a black background, facing screen right. He wears a yellow short-sleeved shirt with a diagonal blue/purple front panel and red sleeve trim, black shorts, white crew socks and white tennis shoes. He holds the racket in his right hand (screen left) and the ball in his left hand (screen right) during the pre-serve routine.

shots.storyline: A single player stands alone under a spotlight on a dark court, bent forward at the waist in a pre-serve routine, racket dangling in his right hand at screen left and ball in his left hand at screen right. From 0.4 s he drives the ball down with his left hand for the first bounce (ball on the floor at ~0.7 s, re-caught by 0.9 s), holds it briefly at waist height (1.0–1.6 s), then repeats a second hand-driven bounce between 1.7 s and 2.3 s (floor contact ~2.0–2.1 s, catch 2.3 s). At 2.4–2.6 s he swings the racket horizontal in front of his body and transfers the ball from his left hand onto the strings, then remains almost motionless in this ball-on-strings holding posture, gazing toward screen right, from ~2.6 s until ~4.9 s. From 5.0 s the left (non-racket) arm lifts the ball off the strings and releases it into the service toss (ball visible as a green blur high above his head at 5.2 s, tossing arm fully extended by 5.3–5.4 s). The racket arm, cocked back low on screen left at 5.5 s, then accelerates upward along the screen-left side (5.6–6.0 s) into an overhead extension (~6.1–6.2 s), after which the racket and arm sweep across and down toward screen right in the follow-through (6.3–7.0 s); his feet appear momentarily off the ground during the strike/extension phase (~6.4–6.7 s) and he lands in a forward lunge facing screen right by ~6.9–7.0 s. From 7.1 s to the end of the clip (7.567 s) he recovers upright and draws the racket back in front of his body with both hands in a ready position. Ball–racket contact itself is never visible in these frames, and the long static ball-on-strings hold between the bounce routine and the toss is recorded only as context, not as a technique.

actions.detail: First pre-serve hand-driven bounce; ball travels vertically down and back up on the screen-right side of the body, near the left leg; body remains crouched and facing screen right.

actions.evidence: Ball held at waist in left hand at 1.7 s, drops to knee (1.8 s), reaches the floor (1.9–2.1 s), rebounds past the knee (2.2 s) and is caught again in the left hand at 2.3 s.
actions.detail: Second pre-serve hand-driven bounce, same vertical path on the screen-right side of the body; immediately after this catch he begins moving the ball toward the racket.

actions.evidence: At 2.4–2.5 s the right hand swings the racket head up to a horizontal position in front of the body while the left hand carrying the ball meets the strings; by 2.6 s the ball rests on the strings with the left hand at the throat, a posture held unchanged through ~4.9 s.
actions.detail: Transfer of the bounced ball onto the racket strings as part of the pre-serve settling routine; no stroke is played. The subsequent static hold (2.6–4.9 s) is outside the technique scope and is not logged separately.

actions.evidence: Parent stroke spanning the toss initiation (left hand lifts ball off strings, 5.0–5.1 s), the release and upward flight of the ball (5.2 s), the racket dropping back and accelerating overhead (5.5–6.2 s), and the sweep across/down to screen right after extension (6.3–7.0 s); feet leave the ground around 6.4–6.7 s and he lands lunging toward screen right by 6.9–7.0 s.
actions.detail: Complete service motion from toss initiation through follow-through; body rises from the crouch, rotates to face screen right, jumps, and finishes with the racket crossing to the screen-right/down side. Ball–racket contact is not directly visible, so contact timing is inferred only from the overhead extension at ~6.1–6.2 s.

actions.evidence: Left (non-racket) hand raises the ball from the strings at 5.0–5.1 s, releases it (ball visible as a green blur above the head at 5.2 s), and the left arm finishes fully extended upward at 5.3–5.4 s.
actions.detail: Non-racket-arm toss rising vertically above the head; ball leaves the hand between 5.1 and 5.2 s.

actions.evidence: Racket arm (right) is cocked back low on screen left at 5.5 s, then the racket traces upward along the screen-left side (5.6–5.9 s) and reaches the overhead position beside the extended tossing arm by 6.0–6.2 s; torso arches backward and head tilts up.
actions.detail: Racket accelerates from the dropped-back position up toward the overhead; equipment trajectory runs from lower screen-left to upper centre; no ball contact is visible in the frames.

actions.evidence: After the overhead extension the racket arm sweeps across the body: arms spread at 6.3–6.4 s, body arched with feet off the ground ~6.4–6.7 s, then the blurred racket and arm continue down and out to the screen-right side (6.8–6.9 s) as the body uncoils into the landing lunge, finishing low at screen right by 7.0 s.
actions.detail: Post-extension continuation of the racket and arm from overhead across to the screen-right/down side; body momentum carries him forward toward screen right, feet returning to the court by ~7.0 s.

uncertainties: Ball–racket contact is never visible in any frame (the served ball leaves the field of view), so the exact instant of contact and any spin cannot be confirmed; the overhead extension at ~6.1–6.2 s is the only proxy.

Motion blur and the ~10 fps sampling make the boundaries between upward swing, contact and follow-through approximate (±0.1 s); the racket still appears high in frames 6.5–6.7 s, so the precise start of the downward sweep is uncertain.
Whether the player truly leaves the ground is suggested by the airborne-looking feet at ~6.4–6.7 s but not sharply resolved.
Only two hand-driven bounces are observable in this clip; earlier or later bounces outside the shot are unknown.
The small chest and shorts logos are present but unreadable at this resolution.
